# Multi-Stage Dockerfile for Node.js TypeScript Application

## Project Structure
```
project/
├── src/
│   └── index.ts
├── package.json
├── package-lock.json
├── tsconfig.json
└── Dockerfile
```

## Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# ============================================================
# Stage 1: Base — shared foundation with common configuration
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS base

# Set working directory for all subsequent stages
WORKDIR /app

# Install dumb-init for proper signal handling and PID 1 management
# This ensures graceful shutdowns work correctly in containers
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

# ============================================================
# Stage 2: Dependencies — install ALL dependencies (dev + prod)
# ============================================================
FROM base AS dependencies

# Copy only package files first to leverage Docker layer caching.
# This layer is only rebuilt when package.json or lock file changes.
COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install all dependencies including devDependencies needed for compilation.
# --frozen-lockfile ensures reproducible builds by failing if lock file
# is out of sync with package.json
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile

# ============================================================
# Stage 3: Builder — compile TypeScript to JavaScript
# ============================================================
FROM dependencies AS builder

# Copy TypeScript configuration
COPY tsconfig.json ./

# Copy source code
COPY src/ ./src/

# Compile TypeScript to JavaScript.
# Output goes to /app/dist as configured in tsconfig.json
RUN npm run build

# ============================================================
# Stage 4: Production Dependencies — install only prod packages
# ============================================================
FROM base AS production-dependencies

COPY package.json package-lock.json ./

# Install ONLY production dependencies, excluding devDependencies.
# This creates a clean, minimal node_modules for the final image.
RUN npm ci --frozen-lockfile --omit=dev

# ============================================================
# Stage 5: Release — final minimal production image
# ============================================================
FROM node:20-alpine AS release

# Install dumb-init in the final stage as well
RUN apk add --no-cache dumb-init

# Create a non-root user and group for security best practices.
# Running as root inside a container is a security risk.
RUN addgroup --system --gid 1001 nodejs && \
    adduser --system --uid 1001 --ingroup nodejs nodeuser

WORKDIR /app

# Copy only what's needed from previous stages:
# 1. Production node_modules from the production-dependencies stage
COPY --from=production-dependencies --chown=nodeuser:nodejs /app/node_modules ./node_modules

# 2. Compiled JavaScript from the builder stage
COPY --from=builder --chown=nodeuser:nodejs /app/dist ./dist

# 3. package.json (needed for npm scripts and metadata)
COPY --chown=nodeuser:nodejs package.json ./

# Switch to non-root user
USER nodeuser

# Document the port the application listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Set NODE_ENV to production for performance optimizations
# (enables Express production mode, disables dev-only features, etc.)
ENV NODE_ENV=production

# Health check to verify the application is running correctly.
# Adjust the endpoint and timing values to match your application.
HEALTHCHECK --interval=30s --timeout=10s --start-period=15s --retries=3 \
    CMD node -e "require('http').get('http://localhost:3000/health', (r) => { \
        process.exit(r.statusCode === 200 ? 0 : 1) \
    }).on('error', () => process.exit(1))"

# Use dumb-init as the entrypoint to handle signals properly.
# It acts as PID 1 and forwards signals to the Node.js process.
ENTRYPOINT ["dumb-init", "--"]

# Start the compiled application
CMD ["node", "dist/index.js"]
```

## Supporting Files

### tsconfig.json
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "target": "ES2022",
    "module": "commonjs",
    "lib": ["ES2022"],
    "outDir": "./dist",
    "rootDir": "./src",
    "strict": true,
    "esModuleInterop": true,
    "skipLibCheck": true,
    "forceConsistentCasingInFileNames": true,
    "resolveJsonModule": true,
    "declaration": true,
    "declarationMap": false,
    "sourceMap": false,
    "removeComments": true,
    "noUnusedLocals": true,
    "noUnusedParameters": true,
    "noImplicitReturns": true
  },
  "include": ["src/**/*"],
  "exclude": ["node_modules", "dist", "**/*.test.ts", "**/*.spec.ts"]
}
```

### package.json
```json
{
  "name": "my-typescript-app",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "description": "Node.js TypeScript application",
  "main": "dist/index.js",
  "scripts": {
    "build": "tsc --project tsconfig.json",
    "start": "node dist/index.js",
    "dev": "ts-node src/index.ts",
    "lint": "eslint src/**/*.ts",
    "test": "jest"
  },
  "dependencies": {
    "express": "^4.18.2"
  },
  "devDependencies": {
    "@types/express": "^4.17.21",
    "@types/node": "^20.10.0",
    "typescript": "^5.3.2"
  },
  "engines": {
    "node": ">=20.0.0"
  }
}
```

### .dockerignore
```dockerignore
# Version control
.git
.gitignore

# Dependencies (will be installed fresh in Docker)
node_modules

# Build output (will be compiled fresh in Docker)
dist

# Development and test files
**/*.test.ts
**/*.spec.ts
**/__tests__
coverage
.nyc_output

# Environment files (use Docker secrets or env vars instead)
.env
.env.*
!.env.example

# Editor and OS files
.vscode
.idea
*.swp
*.swo
.DS_Store
Thumbs.db

# Docker files (not needed inside the image)
Dockerfile
.dockerignore
docker-compose*.yml

# Documentation
README.md
docs/

# CI/CD
.github
.gitlab-ci.yml
```

## Build and Run Commands

```bash
# Build the image
docker build -t my-ts-app:latest .

# Build with specific target stage (useful for debugging)
docker build --target builder -t my-ts-app:debug .

# Run the container
docker run -p 3000:3000 my-ts-app:latest

# Run with environment variables
docker run -p 3000:3000 \
  -e DATABASE_URL=postgres://... \
  -e API_KEY=secret \
  my-ts-app:latest

# Check the final image size
docker images my-ts-app

# Inspect image layers
docker history my-ts-app:latest
```

## Stage Summary

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    Build Pipeline                           │
├──────────────────┬──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Stage            │ Purpose                                  │
├──────────────────┼──────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ base             │ Alpine + dumb-init foundation            │
│ dependencies     │ All deps (dev + prod) for compilation    │
│ builder          │ TypeScript → JavaScript compilation      │
│ prod-deps        │ Production-only node_modules             │
│ release          │ Final image: compiled JS + prod deps     │
└──────────────────┴──────────────────────────────────────────┘

Approximate sizes:
  Full dev image:  ~500MB
  Final image:     ~150MB  (70% reduction)
```

## Key Optimizations Explained

| Technique | Benefit |
|-----------|---------|
| `node:20-alpine` base | ~5MB vs ~900MB for full Debian |
| Multi-stage builds | Dev tools never reach final image |
| `npm ci --frozen-lockfile` | Reproducible, faster installs |
| `--omit=dev` in final stage | Excludes TypeScript, ts-node, etc. |
| `.dockerignore` | Prevents unnecessary files in build context |
| `dumb-init` | Proper signal handling, no zombie processes |
| Non-root user | Security hardening |
| `sourceMap: false` | Smaller compiled output |
| `removeComments: true` | Smaller compiled output |
| Layer ordering | Package files copied before source for cache reuse |
